cues.show: You with the guitar, the CAGED shapes on screen.
cues.say: One chord can be played in five places on the neck. Each place has a shape, named after the open chord it looks like: C, A, G, E and D.

cues.show: Play the open chord, then the same chord in the next shape up the neck.
cues.say: Here is the chord down by the nut. And here it is again higher up, with the next shape. The notes are the same, so it is the same chord.

cues.show: Point at where two shapes meet on the neck: the notes they share.
cues.say: Each shape starts where the one before it ends. The notes they share are how you get from one to the next.

cues.show: On one shape's panel: press Play on the chord, the arpeggio, the pentatonic and the scale.
cues.say: Inside each shape sit four things: the chord, its arpeggio, the pentatonic scale and the full scale. Press Play under each one to hear it.

cues.show: On one shape's panel: press Play on the chord, the arpeggio, the pentatonic and the scale.
cues.say: They all fit under the hand in the same place.

cues.show: Walk the chord up the neck through all five shapes.
cues.say: Play the chord in all five shapes, from the lowest up the neck. Practice until you know where the next shape starts from the one you are in.

cues.show: Press Sample melody. Then play chord, arpeggio and a scale line in one shape without moving.
cues.say: Try things with it. Press Sample melody to hear a short tune made from one shape's notes.

cues.show: Press Sample melody. Then play chord, arpeggio and a scale line in one shape without moving.
cues.say: Stay in one shape and play the chord, then its arpeggio, then a line from the scale, without moving your hand.

cues.show: Press Sample melody. Then play chord, arpeggio and a scale line in one shape without moving.
cues.say: Find the root in each shape and play only the roots, up the neck.
